vram_gb.description: HBM or VRAM per device/package. Multi-die parts: see notes.

memory_bandwidth_basis.description: How the bandwidth figure was derived, e.g. 'GDDR6 28Gbps x 384-bit'.

onchip_cache.description: On-chip cache/SRAM capacity, which is NOT the same quantity as vram_gb and was previously reachable only through free-text notes. Added 2026-10-05 as a structured field because a wave-4 crawler put L2 size into flop.affected_by_hardware - a cross-reference field that could never resolve - and a later pass pushed it back into prose, which made it unqueryable. Where the figure belongs is HERE, on the part that has it. SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, and every sub-field is nullable because the on-chip hierarchy is not comparable across vendors: AMD's Infinity Cache is a package-level LLC sitting in FRONT of HBM, NVIDIA's L2 is a true last-level cache, Tenstorrent's figure is SRAM acting as an L2-like feed tier, and Qualcomm's is on-die SRAM sized to hold weights. Any of those is a real inference-relevant number and none is the same number as the next vendor's. Never sum or compare them across vendors without reading `kind` first. DO NOT FILL A FIELD YOU DID NOT VERIFY against a first-party spec sheet, architecture whitepaper or vendor docs page: a null here is the correct value for a part whose on-chip hierarchy nobody publishes.

kind.description: What the capacity below actually IS. Required whenever the object is non-null, because this is the field that stops a reader treating AMD's Infinity Cache and NVIDIA's L2 as interchangeable. All THREE members are in use as of 2026-10-05: 'l2' 1 record (nvidia-rtx-5090), 'llc-in-front-of-hbm' 3 (MI300X, MI350P, MI355X), 'sram-feed-tier' 1 (tenstorrent-wormhole-n150). A FOURTH member, 'weight-resident-sram', was drafted for Qualcomm AI100/AI200 (whose on-die SRAM is sized to hold weights and is the fastest on-package memory in that family) and then REMOVED unused: the vendor pages behind those two figures could not be re-verified first-party during the 2026-10-05 pass, and adding a kind no record could honestly hold would have been exactly the documented failure mode in this repo - an enum member recognised by zero records. The Qualcomm records keep onchip_cache null, which means 'not verified first-party'. Re-add the member in the same commit as a verified AI100 or AI200 record, never before. 'unknown' and null have ZERO rows: they exist so a generated skeleton and a record whose on-chip hierarchy genuinely could not be identified still validate, matching the convention paper.venue_track and metric_exposure.metric_type use. They are not gaps, and a future pass should not read their emptiness as a reason to invent a row.

l2_kb.description: NVIDIA-style true L2, in KB. Published as e.g. 73728 KB (RTX 4090).

llc_mb.description: Package-level last-level cache in FRONT of HBM, MB. AMD Infinity Cache: 256 MB on MI300X and MI355X, 128 MB on MI350P. Reading time for a hit is HBM-class; on a miss the data has still crossed HBM, so this is a hit-rate multiplier rather than a bandwidth multiplier.

sram_mb.description: On-die SRAM acting as an L2-like feed tier, MB. Tenstorrent Wormhole: 108 MB per n150 card.

per_scope.description: CRITICAL and easy to get wrong. AMD MI300X/MI355X print 4 MB L2 per compute die (XCD) and 256 MB Infinity Cache per 8-XCD PACKAGE - the two numbers describe different scopes and must never be added or compared directly.

basis.description: Provenance of the figure. Only first-party sources are accepted; a secondary aggregator is not recorded here, because a cache size copied from an aggregator is indistinguishable from one copied from a wrong column.

source_note.description: Where the number was read, and any trap found. E.g. the GeForce RTX Blackwell architecture whitepaper prints L2 per FULL DIE (GB203 = 65536 KB) in one table and per SKU in another; the 5070 Ti is 49152 KB, not the full-die 65536 KB, and the RTX 5090 is explicitly called out as 96 MB on a 128 MB GB202.

precision.description: 'fp64' added 2026-10-04: previously every FP64 row was filed as 'other', indistinguishable from a row whose precision nobody knows. 'int16' added the same day for the one Cambricon INT16 TOPS row, which was the other half of the same conflation. 'other' currently has ZERO rows (2026-10-04 audit cleared all 19), and that is the point of the audit rather than a reason to delete the member: it is the only bucket available for a row whose precision is genuinely undetermined, which is a real state - the horizon-journey-6p source states 560 TOPS without naming a precision. It is KEPT for that case. What must not happen is 'other' being used as a parking space for a precision the enum is missing, which is exactly what it was doing for all 16 FP64 rows before 'fp64' was added.

basis.description: REQUIRED on every row. Which kind of statement the number is. This is the per-row *basis* field the repo lacked: a flops[] item used to be able to carry a tflops value with only free-text notes, which is how eight generated values survived review. See basis_detail for the derivation itself. NOTE ON THE ABSENT mlperf-submission VALUE: an 'mlperf-submission' member was drafted here and then REMOVED unused, deliberately. MLPerf Inference submissions report ACHIEVED THROUGHPUT under a named scenario (Offline, Server, Interactive) - they do not report vendor peak tensor-core TFLOPS, which is what a flops[] row holds. The repo holds 49 MLPerf sources and 32 of kind 'benchmark', and NOT ONE of them backs an accelerator flops row, because none of them can. Adding the value would have produced the exact documented failure mode in this repo: an enum member recognised by zero records. Achieved MLPerf throughput belongs in data/benchmarks/, which is where those 32 records already live.

basis_detail.description: The derivation in words, with the numbers substituted: 'HGX B200 column, FP8 row prints 9 PFLOPS under footnote 2 (sparse); dense is one-half -> 4.5 PFLOPS recorded as 4500'. A reader must be able to re-run this with their own numbers.

unit.description: Only when one precision has several distinct hardware paths, e.g. 'fp64-tensor-core' vs 'fp64-vector'. A100 prints both 9.7 and 19.5 TFLOPS FP64 and they are NOT the same path.

sources.description: source ids; each must exist in data/sources/
